task_instance: Given a sample project context (a zombie internal LegacyReportService with 12 consumers, a production-proven ReportsAPI v2 replacement, and a `rpt_owner`->`owner_user_id` column rename needed on the `reports` table), produce a deprecation notice, a consumer migration guide, and a full expand/contract database schema migration plan, following the deprecation-and-migration skill's structure (Deprecation Decision checklist, Advisory/Compulsory choice, Announce-and-Document format, incremental migration per consumer, Expand/Migrate/Contract phases, and the skill's Verification checklists).
evidence: Created project-context.md (sample input describing the legacy system, its 12 consumers, the replacement, and the schema change) and migration-plan.md (the deliverable) in the work directory via the Write tool, then re-read migration-plan.md with the Read tool to confirm it was written correctly. migration-plan.md contains: (1) a worked deprecation-decision analysis answering all 5 questions from the skill and choosing Compulsory deprecation with justification; (2) a formal Deprecation Notice in the skill's exact template format; (3) a step-by-step migration guide with a per-consumer table applying the Churn Rule (team migrates owned cron jobs directly, ad-hoc consumers get guide+deadline+support) and a Step-4 removal checklist; (4) a 5-phase expand/contract schema migration plan (expand nullable column, dual-write, batched backfill, switch reads with bake period, isolated later contract/drop) each with an explicit down/rollback path, matching the skill's rules on additive-first/destructive-last-and-alone and tested down paths; (5) the skill's two Verification checklists filled in, with unmet items honestly left unchecked and explained (they require real production rollout over weeks, not a planning artifact). This is the skill's core stated deliverable -- documentation/planning artifacts (deprecation notices, migration guides, schema migration plans) -- which is pure text authoring achievable with only Write/Read tools; no code execution, binaries, or external services were needed. No shell/Bash, MCP, or connector tools were used. (Note: the skill also covers actually executing migrations -- running scripts, applying schema changes, verifying via production metrics/logs -- which would require code execution and live-system access outside this runtime's abilities; the chosen task instance targets the skill's planning/documentation deliverable, the part directly achievable and verifiable as text here.)
